```{r}
df <- data.frame(
u1 = c(5, 1, 4, NA, NA, NA, 2, 1),
u2 = c(5, NA, 3, 2, 5, NA, 2, 1),
u3 = c(1, 4, 2, 5, 2, NA, 5, 4),
u4 = c(4, 2, NA, 1, 5, 2, 3, 3)
)
```

```{r}
# Problem 1

u2_6 <- mean(df$u2, na.rm = TRUE) + 1 * (df$u4[6] - mean(df$u4, na.rm = TRUE))
u2_6

```


```{r}
# Problem 2
#
#Use Pearson correlation to determine which movie is the most similar to Movie 1.
#(Optional: Google how to use a for loop to speed up this task.)
cor_mat <- cor(t(df), use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "pearson")
movie1 <- cor_mat[-1,1]
# removed the first movie, so need to add 1 to index
movie_num <- which(movie1 == max(movie1, na.rm = TRUE)) + 1
sprintf("Movie %d is most similar to Movie 1.", movie_num)
```

```{r}
countries <- read.csv("https://manctsui.github.io/datasets/countries.csv")
```

```{r}
# Problem 3A
#Apply mean imputation grouped according to region to fill in missing values
#in the column for "Agriculture" and the column for "Industry"
#for the countries dataset

countries |>
  group_by(Region) |> 
  mutate(Agriculture = ifelse(is.na(Agriculture), mean(Agriculture, na.rm = TRUE), Agriculture)) |>
  mutate(Industry = ifelse(is.na(Industry), mean(Industry, na.rm = TRUE), Industry)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  reactable()

# Problem 3B
#How many NA's did you have to fill from each region?
countries |>
  filter(is.na(Agriculture) == TRUE) |> 
  group_by(Region) |>
  count(is.na(Agriculture)) |>
  ungroup()
countries |>
  filter(is.na(Industry) == TRUE) |> 
  group_by(Region) |>
  count(is.na(Industry)) |>
  ungroup()
```


```{r}
#Problem 4
cricket <- data.frame(
temp = c(79, 74, 73, 76, 82, 72, 71, 79, 83, 70, 73, 75, 77),
chirps = c(44, 40, 38, 43, 48, 37, 34, 45, 51, 32, 35, 42, 43)
)

lm(temp ~ chirps, data = cricket)

cor_tc <- cor(cricket$temp, cricket$chirps)
mean_temp <- mean(cricket$temp)
mean_chirps <- mean(cricket$chirps)
sd_temp <- sd(cricket$temp)
sd_chirps <- sd(cricket$chirps)
```

Apply the original lm to cricket
```{r}
cricket <- cricket |> mutate(equ =  0.714 * chirps + 46.474)
```
mean-center then standardize temp and chirps
```{r}
cricket_std <- cricket |>
  mutate(temp = (temp - mean_temp) / sd_temp) |>
  mutate(chirps = (chirps - mean_chirps) / sd_chirps)
```
Then calculate temperature from the correlation between temperature and chirps multiplied by the standardized chirps, then un-apply this standardization for temp.
```{r}
cricket_std <- cricket_std |>
  mutate(equ_std = (cor_tc * chirps) * sd_temp + mean_temp)
```

```{r}
cricket_std
```
Notice the similarity between equ and std_equ.
Thus doing this is equivalent to using lm.
